nodes.title: CLAUDE.md - Claude Code Configuration
nodes.summary: Claude Code configuration file that defines the Understand Anything plugin architecture, commands, conventions, and development workflow for AI-assisted codebase analysis.
nodes.description: This configuration file serves as the authoritative reference for Claude Code when working with the Understand Anything project. It documents the monorepo structure with pnpm workspaces, the core packages (core analysis engine, React dashboard), the skill implementations, and agent definitions. Key sections cover prerequisites (Node.js >= 22, pnpm >= 10), the graph-first dashboard layout with dark luxury theme, the multi-agent pipeline architecture, and essential commands for building, testing, and developing the plugin. The file also explains the versioning strategy across six package.json files and provides detailed instructions for testing local plugin changes by copying to Claude's cache directory.

nodes.title: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md - Community Guidelines
nodes.summary: Community code of conduct establishing respectful communication norms, reporting procedures for violations, and the scope of application across all project spaces.
nodes.description: This document establishes the community guidelines for the Understand Anything project. It emphasizes being respectful, assuming good intent, providing constructive feedback, and keeping discussions on-topic. The document outlines behaviors that are not acceptable, including personal attacks, privacy violations, and sustained disruption. It provides clear reporting procedures using GitHub's private vulnerability reporting system or direct email to maintainers. The code of conduct applies to all project spaces including issues, pull requests, discussions, and commits. The document is intentionally concise, based on the spirit of the Contributor Covenant without verbatim reproduction.

nodes.title: CONTRIBUTING.md - Developer Contribution Guide
nodes.summary: Comprehensive guide for contributors covering setup, development workflow, testing guidelines, code style conventions, and the pull request process for the Understand Anything project.
nodes.description: This extensive contribution guide provides everything developers need to contribute to Understand Anything. It covers multiple contribution types: bug reports, feature requests, documentation, code contributions, and testing. The setup section details prerequisites (Node.js >= 22, pnpm >= 10), forking/cloning the repository, and building the core package. The development workflow section explains branch naming conventions (feat/, fix/, docs/), commit message standards (feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore), and the pull request checklist. Testing guidelines cover Vitest usage, test file organization, and running tests in watch mode. Code style sections address TypeScript strict mode, avoiding `any` types, ESLint usage, and React component patterns. The document also includes file organization structure, translation guidelines for adding new languages, bug report templates, and feature request procedures.

nodes.title: README.md - Project Overview
nodes.summary: Main project documentation introducing Understand Anything as an AI-powered codebase analysis tool that generates interactive knowledge graphs for code exploration.
nodes.description: The main README introduces Understand Anything, an open-source tool that combines LLM intelligence with static analysis to produce interactive dashboards for understanding codebases. The project works across multiple AI coding platforms including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, and more. Key features include: structural graph exploration, business logic domain view, knowledge base analysis, guided tours, fuzzy and semantic search, diff impact analysis, persona-adaptive UI, layer visualization, and language concept explanations. The quick start section explains the three-step process: install the plugin, run `/understand` to analyze the codebase, and use `/understand-dashboard` to explore the interactive visualization. The document details the tree-sitter + LLM hybrid architecture where tree-sitter provides deterministic structural analysis and LLM provides semantic understanding. It documents the multi-agent pipeline with 5-7 specialized agents for project scanning, file analysis, architecture analysis, tour building, graph reviewing, domain analysis, and article analysis. Installation instructions cover native Claude Code installation, shell installers for various platforms, and auto-discovery for Cursor and VS Code with GitHub Copilot.

nodes.title: SECURITY.md - Security Vulnerability Reporting
nodes.summary: Security disclosure policy explaining how to report vulnerabilities, expected response timelines, and the security model's scope as a local-only static analysis tool.
nodes.description: This security document provides guidelines for responsible disclosure of security vulnerabilities in Understand Anything. It outlines two reporting methods: GitHub's private vulnerability reporting (preferred) or opening a regular issue with a 'security:' prefix. The document specifies what to include in reports: issue description, reproduction steps, affected versions, and credit preferences. Expected response timelines are: initial acknowledgement within days, and fix/mitigation plan within ~30 days for confirmed issues. The document emphasizes that this is a local-only static analysis tool that runs on the developer's machine, reads the analyzed project, and writes graphs to the data directory without external communication. It documents the security model: the file-content endpoint is gated by access token and path allowlist, and agents don't execute shell commands from untrusted paths. In-scope issues include code execution from hostile projects, path traversal in the dashboard, and untrusted path handling. Out-of-scope issues include bugs requiring malicious local users with write access or users pasting malicious URLs into the dashboard.
